bounded-context.name: Graph model
bounded-context.purpose: Convert the server's `ResolvedGraph` into a renderable diagram. Build a lens-specific node/edge model from the cold layer, hand it to ELK.js for layout, then render with xyflow. Lenses (ownership / surfaces / code / territory) plus per-lens edge styling, kind filters, and context filters.
bounded-context.narrative:
Three steps and the user sees a diagram. First, `buildModel(graph, lens, opts)` projects into a flat list of s and s — the decides which entities become nodes and which relationships become edges. Containers (bounded-contexts and shared-kernels in the ownership lens, surfaces in the surfaces lens) handle the compound-graph nesting. The set of lenses is closed at the type level ().
Second, ELK lays it out — given the same model and options, the same positions come out every time (). Filter toggles rebuild the model and re-run layout rather than fading nodes in place (): the editorial choice is "the diagram reshapes," not "things slide around."
Third, xyflow renders the with the editorial aesthetic (custom nodes, four-corner cluster ticks). Nothing graph-specific lives on the server: the graph view consumes the same `LexiconResponse` the reading room does ().

term.name: lens
term.definition: A named projection of the `ResolvedGraph` answering one structural question. Two exist: **ownership** (bounded contexts and shared kernels as compound containers with their owned atoms — terms, invariants, seams, boundary rules, aggregates, modules — nested inside, primary lens), and **surfaces** (surfaces as containers with regions nested). The lens is part of the URL: `/p/:id/graph/<lens>`.
term.equality: By string value (`"ownership" | "surfaces"`). Two lens values are the same iff their strings match.

term.name: GraphNode
term.definition: One node in the renderable graph model: `{id, kind, name, parent?, isCluster?, width, height}`. `id` is the entity's fqid (or a synthetic `__cluster/...` for cross-cutting / ADR pseudo-containers). `parent` makes it a child in a compound graph. Width/height are pre-layout size hints — set to 0 for containers (ELK computes from children).

term.name: GraphEdge
term.definition: One typed edge in the model: `{id, source, target, kind, label?, directed}`. `kind` is one of `disambiguates | seam | boundary-rule | contains | narrative`; each kind is rendered with its own aesthetic (solid oxide / dashed vellum / dotted saffron / arrow style). Two vestigial kinds (`affects`, `supersedes`) survive in the type union for compatibility with the v0.2 fanout-routing infrastructure but are never emitted under v0.3 since ADRs were removed.

term.name: cluster node
term.definition: A synthetic compound-graph container that holds entities sharing no bounded context but belonging together visually. In v0.3 the primary use is for layout sub-grouping inside the ownership lens; the v0.2 cross-cutting and decisions clusters are gone (shared kernels now render as real compound containers, ADRs were removed). Distinguished from real bounded-context containers by `kind: "cluster"` and the `__cluster/` id prefix.

term.name: affects routing
term.definition: Vestigial strategy for drawing ADR→entity `affects` edges from v0.2, later reused as narrative polyline tactics (HEB / A* / elbow). Removed when xyflow became the only canvas — ELK places nodes, xyflow draws edges, so there is no layout-side path router left.

term.name: LayoutResult
term.definition: What ELK produces and the canvas consumes: a flat list of `PositionedNode`s (with `x, y` plus the original GraphNode fields) and the model's edges (source/target/kind — xyflow routes them). The viewport size is implied by the bounding box of positioned nodes.

invariant.name: lens set is closed
invariant.statement: The `LENSES` array is the complete, ordered list of supported lenses. A `Lens` value outside this set is impossible at the type level; runtime parsing of the URL lens param falls back to "ownership" if the route segment doesn't match.
invariant.rationale: Adding a fourth lens is intentionally heavier than a config edit — it requires new `build<Lens>` logic, new filter semantics, possibly new edge styling. Closing the set prevents accidental drift and makes the surface area easy to enumerate in code review.

invariant.name: layout is deterministic per (model, options)
invariant.statement: Given the same `GraphModel`, ELK produces the same node positions. There is no per-session randomness and no saved layout state. xyflow lets the user drag nodes in the session; that does not persist.
invariant.rationale: Determinism is what lets filter toggles "reshape the diagram" rather than "animate to a new state" — reproducibility comes for free, and the user never has to fight a layout they didn't choose. Adding free-form drag-to-reposition would break this invariant; see `plans/_archive/graph-view/spec.md` non-goals.

invariant.name: filter changes re-run layout
invariant.statement: Toggling kind filters, context filters, or edge filters rebuilds the `GraphModel` and re-runs `layoutModel`. There is no fade-in-place or fade-out animation for filtered-out nodes.
invariant.rationale: ELK is fast enough on graphs of expected size (~50 entities for the sample, hundreds for real projects). Re-layout produces a cleaner diagram than partial-hide-and-reflow, and the editorial aesthetic is "the diagram reshapes" rather than "things slide around."

seam.name: ResolvedGraph → GraphModel
seam.description: The graph view consumes the same `LexiconResponse` the reading room does; nothing graph-specific lives on the server. `buildModel(graph, lens, opts)` is the boundary — every lens reads only typed fields of `ResolvedEntity` (containedTerms, containedAggregates, regions, seam kind, narrative refs …), never the raw XML.
seam.rationale: Conformist: graph-model takes lexicon-loading's `ResolvedGraph` shape as-is, no translation layer. The reading room consumes the same shape; graph-model deliberately stays downstream of the resolved-graph vocabulary rather than introducing its own intermediate model.
